sections.text: Why Wind Damage Needs Immediate Attention in Millcreek

Gusty winds common in the Millcreek corridor can lift shingles, loosen fasteners, and compromise flashing around chimneys and vents. Even minor uplift creates pathways for water during rain or snowmelt. Early inspection prevents interior damage and costly structural repairs. Frame Roofing Utah responds 24/7 to storm events across Millcreek neighborhoods including Canyon View and Millcreek Canyon.
Common Signs of Wind-Related Roof Damage

Look for curled or missing shingles, dented gutters, and debris trapped in valleys. Check ridge caps for displacement and flashing for separation at roof-plane intersections. Interior signs include water stains near attic rafters or ceiling corners. These issues often appear subtly after wind events but can lead to significant leaks if ignored. Frame’s inspectors document all findings with photos for insurance clarity.

howto.name: How to Spot Wind Damage on Your Roof

steps.name: Visual Ground Check
steps.text: Use binoculars to inspect for lifted shingles, dented gutters, or displaced flashing from the ground. Look for debris in valleys or near vents.

steps.name: Attic Inspection
steps.text: Check for water stains, damp insulation, or light leaks in the attic after wind events. These signs often appear before interior damage becomes visible.
